title: High Precision Antibody-Free Microtubule Labeling for Expansion Microscopy
author: Rajdeep Chowdhury
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: HeLa cells were used in this protocol for microtubule extraction and subsequent labeling using NHS-ester chemistry Reagents
Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium (DMEM) (Gibco, catalog number:
Piperazine-(N,N’-bis(2-ethanesulfonic acid) (PIPES) sodium salt (Merck, catalog number: P
Phalloidin (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: P
Electron microscopy–grade glutaraldehyde solution (50%) (Merck, catalog number: G
Acryloyl-X SE (succinimidyl ester) (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: A
Fluorescein NHS ester (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number:

steps.title: Prepare PIPES stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 32.43 g PIPES sodium salt in 450 mL ddH₂O, add 1 M KOH until fully dissolved, bring volume to 500 mL, adjust pH to 6.9, store at 4 °C (short‑term) or –20 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Prepare MgCl2 stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.476 g MgCl₂·6H₂O in 500 mL ddH₂O to obtain 10 mM, store at 4 °C (short‑term) or –20 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Prepare CaCl2 stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.1 g CaCl₂·2H₂O in 20 mL ddH₂O to obtain 500 mM, store in a 50 mL centrifuge tube at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare EGTA stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.76 g EGTA in 200 mL ddH₂O to obtain 10 mM, store at 4 °C (short‑term) or –20 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Make PEM buffer (100 mM)
steps.instruction: Mix 250 mL PIPES stock (200 mM), 50 mL MgCl₂ stock (10 mM) and 50 mL EGTA stock (10 mM); add 150 mL ddH₂O, adjust pH to 6.9 with 1 M KOH while stirring, final concentrations: 100 mM PIPES, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM EGTA; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Taxol stock (1 mM)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg Taxol in 1.17 mL anhydrous DMSO, aliquot 10 µL, store at –20 °C; keep on ice and avoid repeated thaw‑freeze.

steps.title: Prepare Phalloidin stock (1 mM)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg phalloidin in 1.25 mL anhydrous DMSO, store at –20 °C; aliquots may be reused.

steps.title: Prepare extraction solution (50 mL)
steps.instruction: In 48.8 mL PEM buffer add 2 g PEG 20000, 1 mL Triton X‑100 (2 % v/v), 100 µL Taxol stock (2 µM final), and 100 µL phalloidin stock (2 µM final); mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare fixation solution (0.5 % glutaraldehyde)
steps.instruction: Dilute EM‑grade glutaraldehyde (50 %) to 0.5 % (v/v) in 100 mM PEM buffer, adjust to pH 7.3; prepare fresh immediately before use.

steps.title: Prepare Acryloyl‑X SE stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 mg Acryloyl‑X SE in 500 µL anhydrous DMSO to obtain 10 mg mL⁻¹, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare digestion buffer (100 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.2 g Tris base in 99 mL ddH₂O, add 400 µL 500 mM CaCl₂ stock (final 2 mM), adjust pH to 8.0; then add 500 µL Triton X‑100 (0.5 % v/v) and 7.6 g guanidine‑HCl (800 mM), stir until clear; store at –20 °C in 1.5 mL aliquots, avoid repeated freeze‑thaw.

steps.title: Prepare digestion solution with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Thaw digestion buffer, incubate at 37 °C for 30 min; add Proteinase K (800 U mL⁻¹ stock) 1:100 to obtain 8 U mL⁻¹ working solution; use 2 mL per well of a 6‑well plate or 600 µL per well of a 12‑well plate, ensuring complete gel immersion.

steps.title: Prepare sodium bicarbonate buffer (100 mM)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4.2 g sodium bicarbonate in 500 mL ddH₂O, adjust pH to 8.0, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescein NHS‑ester stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g fluorescein NHS‑ester in 5 mL anhydrous DMSO to obtain 0.2 g mL⁻¹ (200 mg mL⁻¹); store in a tightly sealed amber bottle at 15–30 °C, protect from light, aliquot 50–100 µL, keep at –20 °C, use within 3 months.

steps.title: Culture HeLa cells on coverslips
steps.instruction: Grow HeLa cells in DMEM supplemented with 10 % (v/v) FBS and 100 U mL⁻¹ penicillin‑streptomycin at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; split with 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA when ~95 % confluent; seed cells onto 15 mm round coverslips placed in a 12‑well plate and incubate overnight to reach ~95 % confluency.

steps.title: Detergent extraction and fixation
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium carefully, wash cells with pre‑warmed PBS (37 °C), add extraction solution and incubate 7 min at 37 °C; wash 3 × with PEM buffer at room temperature; fix with freshly prepared 0.5 % glutaraldehyde solution for 20 min at room temperature; wash 3 × with PBS (pH 7.4); wash 3 × with sodium bicarbonate buffer (5 min each).

steps.title: Fluorescent NHS‑ester labeling of cells
steps.instruction: Dilute fluorescein NHS‑ester stock 1 000‑fold in sodium bicarbonate buffer (final ≈0.2 µg mL⁻¹); incubate cells at room temperature for 30 min; wash 3 × with PBS while gently shaking (10 min each); mount coverslip on a glass slide with 5 µL water and image by fluorescence microscopy.

steps.title: Anchor proteins with acryloyl‑X SE
steps.instruction: Incubate coverslips overnight at 4 °C in PBS (pH 7.4) containing 0.3 mg mL⁻¹ acryloyl‑X SE (3 % of the 10 mg mL⁻¹ stock); the next morning wash 3 × with PBS.

steps.title: Gelation of anchored samples
steps.instruction: Place 80 µL gel monomer solution onto parafilm, invert the coverslip with anchored cells onto the droplet, seal in a custom humidified chamber to prevent edge drying, and incubate at room temperature for 12 h.

steps.title: Detach gels and transfer to plate
steps.instruction: Carefully peel the polymerized gel from the parafilm, transfer it into a 6‑well plate, ensuring the gel remains intact.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion of gels
steps.instruction: Add 1 000 µL digestion solution to each gel, incubate for 20 h at 37 °C (gel expands ~3‑fold).

steps.title: Post‑digestion NHS‑ester labeling of gel
steps.instruction: Transfer gel to a 60 mm Petri dish, wash 3 × with 100 mM sodium bicarbonate buffer; prepare labeling solution by adding 10 µL fluorescein NHS‑ester stock (0.2 mg mL⁻¹) to 10 mL bicarbonate buffer, vortex vigorously, add to the dish, and incubate 30 min on a gentle low‑speed shaker.

steps.title: Expand gels in water
steps.instruction: Move the gel to a dedicated expansion chamber and wash it at least six times with ddH₂O until fully expanded to ~15 cm diameter (≈4‑20× expansion depending on polymer composition).

steps.title: Mount expanded gel for imaging
steps.instruction: Assemble the custom chamber (aluminum holder for a 22 × 40 mm #1.5 coverslip) by applying a thin grease layer, placing the supporting net, and securing the lid; blot excess water from the gel, determine orientation, flip if the sample is on the top surface, place gel onto the net, trim edges with a weighing‑tray piece for a snug fit, and close the chamber firmly.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images (non‑expanded & expanded)
steps.instruction: For non‑expanded samples use an Olympus IX71 epifluorescence microscope with a 100× 1.41 NA oil objective, F‑view II CCD (64.5 nm pixel). For expanded samples use a Leica TCS SP5 STED in confocal mode (488 nm or 633 nm excitation, 100× 1.4 NA STED objective, HyD detectors, AOTF, 8 kHz scan, 8‑bit, 128 × 128 pixels, 98 nm pixel size). For 3‑D STED acquire on a Leica STELLARIS 8 with a 100× 1.4 NA STED White objective, white‑light laser, 80 MHz pulse frequency, 775 nm STED beam >1.5 W (50 nm xy vortex, 130 nm z donut), Power HyD detectors, 3× notch filter, using photon‑counting or τSTED mode as required.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in Chowdhury et al. [15] and Shaib et al. [18]. The extraction procedure was validated by observing the non-expanded, extracted cells with NHS-ester under the microscope. Objects closely resembling cytoskeletal elements were easily recognized, which validates the extraction procedure. To validate accurate labeling after expansion, we compared fluorescence images of extracted microtubules in non-expanded cells (Figure 1) with those in expanded cells (Figure 4). The resemblance was obvious, indicating successful labeling. Furthermore, when we analyzed the expanded images at higher resolution using ONE microscopy [8], the filaments precisely matched the expected microtubule patterns. This observation was further supported by line scan analyses, which yielded average profiles of 24.98 nm [15]. This measurement aligns perfectly with previous data obtained from X-ray [16] and CryoEM [17] studies, providing strong evidence for the expansion factor accuracy of the expanded specimens.
